narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 95.8% chance that you would fail the bar exam on the first attempt. In practical terms, the review treated that very high predicted risk as outweighing your admission case, even though this is a prediction rather than a certainty.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing: you were in the lowest decile, while accepted students averaged near the middle of their class. That low standing pushed the prediction strongly toward bar-exam failure. Your first-year class standing was the next most influential factor; at the second decile, it was also much lower than the accepted-student average around the sixth decile, adding further risk. Your Law School Admission Test score of 28, compared with an accepted average of about 37, was the third most important factor and also pushed toward failure. Gender and race were not used in the prediction.

To improve a future application, focus on showing that you can handle bar-level work. Consider rigorous additional coursework or academic remediation, prepare to retake the Law School Admission Test if feasible, and meet with an admissions or academic advisor about a concrete improvement plan. You might also ask whether conditional admission or delayed entry is possible. Reapply when you can present stronger academic and test evidence.
